text:
tanya: Heads up — seeing an odd pattern in eu-west1 this morning: GPUs are free according to alloc map but pods remain pending and scheduler keeps evicting tiny helper pods.

kevin: sounds like fragmentation + taint propagation? which pools affected?

tanya: mostly rack-2 and rack-5 in eu-west1a. network probes show normal, but kube events show repeated 'node not ready' around the same time window then immediate recovery. the scheduler tries to place, fails affinity checks, then preempts tiny-containers.

josh: can you paste the kube events and the allocator snapshot?

tanya: pasted small excerpt: 
```
Normal  05:12:03  kubelet  NodeNotReady  node/eu-west1a-rack2-03  KubeletNotReady: heartbeat lost
Normal  05:12:05  scheduler  FailedScheduling  pod=helper-epoch-12  0/24 nodes are available: 24 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
Normal  05:12:06  provisioner  preempt  pod=helper-epoch-12 evicting=cache-loader-9
Normal  05:12:10  kubelet  NodeReady node/eu-west1a-rack2-03  kubelet is now healthy
```

kevin: aha. taints being applied transiently during the kubelet NotReady window then not removed in time before scheduling decisions. leads to ephemeral orphaned GPUs and then scheduler preempts small pods to make room — exacerbates fragmentation.

infra-bot: alert: eu-west1 gpu-pending-fragmentation high — triggered at 2026-02-17T05:12:02Z

josh: mitigation options: 1) lengthen taint TTL on node-not-ready controller from 5s -> 30s? 2) add a 'taint-stable' gate where the scheduler ignores taints younger than X seconds for gang/packed workloads; 3) improve allocator to prefer warm nodes with existing residency.

tanya: 1 might mask real unready nodes. 2 sounds promising: we already do preferring warm nodes for large gangs but not for tiny helpers. the tiny helpers are getting preempted because they don't tolerate the transient taint.

kevin: short term: create a patch to the provisioner to add a small tolerance annotation for system-helper pods so they're less likely to be evicted during brief node NotReady blips. roll that to eu-west1a racks only as a canary.

sre-bot: deploy/provisioner-config v3.2.1 promoted to eu-west1 by @kevin at 2026-02-17T05:28Z

josh: also propose we expose metric: transientTaintRate and taintAgeHistogram so we can set a rule instead of guesswork. plus a gauge of fragmentedGPUCount by rack.

tanya: opened infra-7312 with traces and allocation dumps. adding suggested metrics in the ticket.

kevin: followups: 1) canary tolerate annotation for helper pods, 2) scheduler ignore-young-taints flag for packing-sensitive queues, 3) alarm to alert when fragmentedGPUCount > 8 for any rack for > 10m.

josh: cost note: when the helper pods get preempted we see short-lived re-schedules that spin up spot replacements for dependent workloads. this bumped egress and instance churn — preliminary cost delta ~0.35% over the 20m window in eu-west1. include in postmortem.

infra-bot: alert cleared: eu-west1 gpu-pending-fragmentation low — duration 16m

tanya: rolling canary applied to rack-2. monitoring now. will revert if we see unexpected side-effects. thanks all :thumbsup:
